conventions.convention: Z, A and A(z) are binary; every Y(a,z) is integrable; 0 < P(Z=1) < 1. Potential values have the stated no-interference and single-treatment-version scope.

Consistency, exclusion, joint instrument independence, relevance and monotonicity are separate conditions. Independence concerns the entire potential-value tuple and is defined even without exclusion.
For integrable X and P(B)>0, E[X|B] means E[1_B X]/P(B); conditional means on null events are not defined.
Compliers have (A(0),A(1))=(0,1), defiers have (1,0), and C={A(1)>A(0)}. Under exclusion, ATE=E[Y(1)-Y(0)] and LATE=E[Y(1)-Y(0)|C] only when P(C)>0.
Both observed contrasts subtract instrument level 0 from level 1. The Wald ratio is ΔY/ΔA and requires an integrable observed outcome and ΔA≠0.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the binary IV potential-value setup, integrability and positive instrument atoms, and separately defines consistency, exclusion, joint instrument independence, relevance, monotonicity and event-conditioned means.
Under consistency, exclusion and joint instrument independence, with τ=Y(1)-Y(0), ΔA=E[A(1)-A(0)] and ΔY=E[(A(1)-A(0))τ]. No monotonicity or relevance is needed.
Under binary monotonicity A(1)≥A(0) almost surely, always-takers, never-takers and compliers are pairwise disjoint and cover Ω up to a null set; the defier event has probability zero.
Under consistency, joint instrument independence and monotonicity in the binary IV setup, ΔA=P(C). If the instrument is relevant, then P(C)>0.
Under consistency, exclusion, joint instrument independence and monotonicity, ΔY=E[1_C τ]. If P(C)>0, this equals P(C)E[τ|C].

For a nonempty class of full-data laws satisfying the binary IV setup, consistency, exclusion, joint instrument independence, relevance and monotonicity, the Wald ratio is defined and equals Eθ[Y(1)-Y(0)|C]. Thus LATE is identifiable in the induced observed-data model; equality with the population ATE is not asserted.

published_dependencies.used_for: Measurability and real-valued random-variable conventions in the IV setup.
Finite expectations of integrable potential outcomes.
Joint instrument independence through generated sigma-algebras.
Event-probability factorization in the first-stage proof.
Independence of potential-value functions and instrument indicators.
Measurability of binary-selected potential outcomes and their contrasts.
Subtracting potential-outcome means and extracting constant treatment effects.
Treating ATE and LATE as functions of full-data-law parameters.
Equal observed laws must imply equal target values; the counterexample violates this implication for ATE.
Checking the parameter-to-observed-law interpretation underlying the identification definitions.
Checking that observational equivalence means equality of the entire sampling law.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and its potential-outcome/consistency and causal-effect definitions against the IV setup and identification arguments. Treatment-version scope, almost-sure consistency, integrable ATE contrasts and observed-law identification agree. The IV setup explicitly imposes its own no-interference scope and instrument assumptions; it does not import treatment exchangeability or standardization as an IV premise.
